components.css: .ds-gcard{display:flex;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--border,#e3e3df);border-radius:14px;background:var(--surface,#ffffff);text-decoration:none;color:inherit;transition:transform 200ms ease-out, box-shadow 200ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out}.ds-gcard:hover{transform:translateY(-2px);box-shadow:0 10px 24px -8px rgba(24,26,41,0.14);border-color:var(--border-strong,#d2d2cc)}.ds-gcard:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ring,#7c3aed);outline-offset:2px}.ds-gcover{position:relative;aspect-ratio:3/4;background:var(--surface-2,#f4f4f2);overflow:hidden}.ds-gcover img{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;transition:transform 300ms ease-out}.ds-gcard:hover .ds-gcover img{transform:scale(1.03)}.ds-gver{position:absolute;top:8px;inset-inline-start:8px;padding:2px 10px;border-radius:999px;background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--accent-soft,#f2ecfe) 85%, transparent);color:var(--accent,#6d28d9);font-size:12px;font-weight:500;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;backdrop-filter:blur(4px)}.ds-gbody{display:flex;flex:1;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;padding:12px 14px}.ds-gtitle{font-size:14px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.4;color:var(--foreground,#14151a);display:-webkit-box;-webkit-line-clamp:2;-webkit-box-orient:vertical;overflow:hidden}.ds-gcard:hover .ds-gtitle{color:var(--accent,#6d28d9)}.ds-gmeta{margin-top:auto;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;font-size:12px;color:var(--muted,#5b6070);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-dl{width:14px;height:14px}

narrative.overview: ArgusArGames is a games catalogue that presents Arabic localizations with the composure of a sharp, well-set magazine rather than the dark-neon gaming default. Visitors land looking for one game and a fresh download; the interface removes friction — a working search leads every public page, covers carry the personality, and numbers read as calm data. Light is the committed first environment (paper-white, cool ink, one vivid violet accent), with a system-following dark theme as a first-class equal, not a degraded afterthought. The voice is confident but quiet: restraint in decoration, confidence in order. Both languages are equal citizens — Arabic-first, RTL and English LTR mirror correctly in component, grid, and microcopy.
keyCharacteristics: Cool ink neutrals on paper; violet action accent; amber data accent.
Hairline line + tonal step separation; faint hover lift only.
One authored entrance (rise) per viewport; reduced-motion fully honored.
Tabular numerals on all counts and versions.
Cairo (Arabic) + Inter (Latin) pair, tuned tracking, max text measure ~65-75ch.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Route Violet is used only where the visitor can do something — the primary action, a link, focus, active nav, a pressed vote. It never decorates. Its rarity is what makes "download" impossible to miss.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Every count, version number, and date reads with tabular-nums, so columns of downloads and votes stay calm and comparable row to row.

rules.name: The Search-First Rule
rules.body: The first thing a returning visitor hits on the home page after the headline is the working search; wherever a catalogue appears, search and sort live above the grid, never below it.

rules.name: The Line-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A flat surface at rest is separated by its hairline border. If a card floats, it is telling the visitor it can be acted on — keep that meaning rare and intentional.

dos: Do lead public views with the working search — it is the fastest path to the visitor's game.
Do keep violet scarce: it marks the action spot, nothing else.
Do render every count and version number with tabular numerals.
Do give both languages equal fidelity, including mirrored chevrons and layout via logical properties.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion with the shared reduced-motion block.
donts: Don't import dark-neon gaming tropes — glitch type, heavy gradients, or a neon glow palette.
Don't let cards rest on shadows; separation is a hairline at rest and lift only on press-ready states.
Don't use amber for interactive actions — it designates warm data (most-downloaded, warnings), while violet handles every action.
Don't break the 3:4 cover silhouette on catalogue cards.
Don't add more than one authored entrance animation per viewport.
